title: Ethiopian Guava Juice
community: Ethiopian juice bars — the vitamin C powerhouse juice
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Guava Juice — fresh guavas blended with water and strained to remove seeds, sweetened with honey and a squeeze of lemon. Guava contains more vitamin C than oranges — this simple juice is one of the most nutritious available.
longDesc: Ethiopian guava grows in the highlands and Rift Valley areas — the white-fleshed and pink-fleshed varieties both produce excellent juice. At 4x the vitamin C of oranges per gram, guava juice is the most vitamin-C-dense fruit drink available.
steps: Blend guava quarters with 1 cup water until smooth.
Strain through a fine sieve — press firmly to extract all juice.
chefTips: Strain thoroughly — guava seeds are very hard.
Pink-fleshed guava produces a more beautiful colour.
cookingScience: Guava has 4x more vitamin C per gram than oranges — the Ethiopian highland varieties are particularly concentrated. The blending process does not significantly destroy vitamin C as long as it is consumed quickly (oxidation begins rapidly once the cells are broken).
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian guava grown in home gardens without chemical inputs.
servedWith: During illness as a vitamin C source
culturalNote: Ethiopian guava juice is the community's vitamin C supplement — drunk at juice bars as a morning health boost, given to sick family members, and prepared for children as a natural immunity drink.
